tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

schema.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

content.text:
I've checked the plugin and it matches UE 5.8, so we can go ahead. The zip is DLSS 4.5 plugin **v8.9.0** (NGX 310.9.16), its `EngineVersion` is `5.8.0`, and NVIDIA's guide lists 5.8 as supported.

**Time is the problem.** It's 22:10 UTC now and the jam closes at 01:59 UTC, so we have about 3 h 50 min. The full process (grill, tickets, TDD) plus two packages and an itch push won't fit in that.

- **Plan:** I'll add only `DLSS` and `StreamlineNGXCommon` to `Plugins/`. Those are the two plugins Super Resolution needs, per NVIDIA's table. I'll leave out the 1.6 GB of `.pdb` debug files and `Intermediate/`.
- **Tests:** the SETTINGS row and fallback get a `Jam.` test first, as the project rules require.
- **Cutoff:** if the packaged build doesn't work by about 01:00 UTC, I'll stop and leave main untouched.

Reply **3** and I'll start now with no grill or tickets (recommended), or pick 1 or 2 knowing the build probably won't land before the deadline.

# C++ standard of the jam project

Ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld standards before the jam start. It holds working conventions only: no
game design. A new rule is added here only by the author's decision.

## Style

- Epic C++ Coding Standard + `.clang-format` in the root: tabs, Allman, braces always, `ColumnLimit: 140`.
  `check_code.py` checks the format, never align by hand.
- Comments and commit messages in English only.
- A comment describes the behaviour that exists, not the intended one. Change the behaviour, fix the comment in the
  same commit.
- Epic prefixes: `b` for bool, `F/U/A/E/I` for types.

## Decomposition

- A decision (who is hit, how much damage, what a rule allows, when the run ends) lives in a pure
  `namespace <Feature>Rules` with no world and no actors: `Public/<System>/<Feature>Rules.h`, free functions with
  `JAMGAME_API`, and a header line `Tests: Jam.<Area>.*`.
- An actor, component or subsystem only glues: collects inputs, calls the rule, applies the result.
- A big class is split into `.cpp` files by responsibility with one shared `.h`.
- Soft thresholds: a `.cpp` over ~600 lines, a function over ~60, nesting over 3. Exceeding one is a signal, not a
  ban: split or justify.

## Systems and dependencies

- Folders `Public/<System>` and `Private/<System>`, plus `Tests`.
- **The simulation does not know about the presentation.** `Core` and `Sim` never include `View`, `UI` or `Audio`.
  The directions are forbidden in the `check_code.py` ratchet (`SIMULATION`, `PRESENTATION`): extend both lists when
  a new system folder appears.
- Balance numbers (prices, health, damage, timings) live in data, not in code.
- Randomness of the simulation comes from a seeded stream, not `FMath::Rand`, so a run can be replayed in a test.

## Logs

- No `LogTemp` in new code. Use the category of the system or `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY_STATIC` for a single file.
- Warning and Error only for a breakage or a wrong setup; state changes are `Verbose`, per-tick traces `VeryVerbose`.

## Tests

- Every new decision in `*Rules` gets a test `Jam.<Area>.<Case>` before the code (test first). Glue with the engine
  is checked in PIE, a test is optional.
- The number of `Jam.` tests only grows; a failing test means reverting the change, not bending the test to the code.
- A bug is fixed separately from a refactoring, test first.

## Blueprint seam

- A new Blueprint exposure is opened when needed, not "just in case".
- Logic is not duplicated between an EventGraph and C++: the decision is in C++, the Blueprint only calls.
- Renaming a `UCLASS`/`UPROPERTY`/`UFUNCTION` visible in Blueprints only with CoreRedirects.
- Deletions (C++, assets) only through a dry run with counts and the author's explicit yes.

param([string]$Extra = "", [int]$Seconds = 25)
# Runs the packaged Development game of the dlssrel worktree, then greps its log for DLSS and NGX lines.
$root = "F:\Unreal_Engine\UnrealProjects\MegaJam2026_dlssrel\Saved\Packaged\Windows\JamGame"

Remove-Item $log -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$p = Start-Process -FilePath (Join-Path $root "Binaries\Win64\JamGame.exe") -ArgumentList "-windowed -resx=1280 -resy=720 -nosplash $Extra" -PassThru
Start-Sleep -Seconds $Seconds
if ($p.HasExited) { Write-Output "[smoke] exited by itself, code $($p.ExitCode)" } else { Write-Output "[smoke] running after $Seconds s"; $p | Stop-Process -Force }
Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
Select-String -Path $log -Pattern "DLSS Super Resolution|NGX.*(supported|Init|DLSS)|LogDLSS.*(Error|Warning|supported)|Fatal|Unhandled" | Select-Object -First 15 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(220, $_.Line.Length)) }

![How to play](howtoplay.png)

## Credits

- [Pavlo Vynychenko: direction, design, ... (Team Owner)]
- [Teammate 2: role]
- [Teammate 3: role]

## Tools used

- **Claude Code** (Anthropic, Claude Opus): all C++ code written test-first (299 automated tests), the tickets,
  builds and packaging, headless asset imports, this page's first draft and the dev log.
- **Unreal Engine 5.8** with its MCP toolsets: the agent drove the editor for the Niagara effects and the poses.
- **fal**: OpenAI GPT Image 2.6 (concepts, the opening comic, the menu skyline, the cover), Tencent Hunyuan3D v3
  (katana, shuriken, cash stack), Meshy 7.1 through fal (the Publisher's model).
- **Meshy** API: the hero's model and rig, animation library clips, the shrine props.
- **ElevenLabs**: sound effects, the music and its stems, the ambient loop, the two designed voices and 26 voiced
  lines.
- **PBRgen**: the wet slate floor material.
- **Hyper3D Rodin** Gen-2.5: the arena's stone lanterns
- **Blender 5.2**, run headless by our scripts: the Publisher's rig rebuild, the clip and export fixes.
- **ffmpeg**, **butler**, clang-format.

## Third-party assets

No marketplace assets. AI-generated content is ours and listed in THIRD_PARTY.md of the repository with its tool
and terms. From outside:

- Unreal Engine 5.8 basic shapes (`/Engine/BasicShapes`): Unreal Engine EULA.
- unreal-mcp-bridge (github.com/exetorius/unreal-mcp-bridge, MIT): a relay between Claude Code and the editor's MCP
  server; a tool, not in the game.

## Made before the jam

Only tooling, no game content (the full list is PREJAM.md in the repository): an empty UE 5.8 C++ project, the build

  with the volumes. A level scales numbers the fight already has (hero health, his damage, the cash stack's heal, the
  Publisher's damage), one block per level in `[JamBalance]`; NORMAL is all ones. A retry and PLAY AGAIN keep it. The
  bot wins 60 of 60 on every level: EASY's closest win 148 of 180 health, NORMAL 72 of 120 as before, HARD 4 of 96, so
  the author's starting scales stay. 312 tests, five new, red first. Tools: Claude Code.

  that EASY differs from NORMAL.

  no smoke run, pushed as session-6a to pavyny/ronin-final-cut (build 2399032). The first package failed: a new
  local, `LabelScale`, hid the how-to's constant in the Shipping unity build; renamed.

# NVIDIA RTX Award: answers for the jam form

**Which NVIDIA technology did you use?**
NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution, through the official NVIDIA DLSS plugin for Unreal Engine 5.8 (v8.9.0, NGX
310.9.16). It runs NVIDIA's transformer model; on our card NGX picked its default preset K for QUALITY mode.

**How is it used in the game?**
SETTINGS has an NVIDIA DLSS row: OFF, QUALITY, BALANCED, PERFORMANCE. On an RTX card it is on by default in QUALITY:
the game renders at the mode's optimal resolution (66.7 % in QUALITY) and DLSS upscales it to the screen, so the
Lumen-lit arena keeps its frame rate at high resolutions. The choice is saved with the other settings. On a card
without DLSS (or with an old driver) the row offers only OFF and the game renders exactly as before.

**On what GPU did you develop and test it?**
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER, Windows 11. Checked in the packaged game: DLSS-SR active (`r.NGX.DLSS.Enable 1`,
screen percentage 66.7), and the game also starts and runs with DLSS forced off.

Tools used: **NVIDIA DLSS 4.5** Super Resolution (official UE 5.8 plugin), on by default on RTX cards.

# RONIN: FINAL CUT (itch page text)

Paste-ready text for pavyny/ronin-final-cut. Lines in [square brackets] are for you to fill or check before
publishing; delete the brackets.

---

## Hook

> **RE: your game**
>
> Kid. Loved it. The neon, the rain, the sword guy. Love it.
> Now cut it in half and ship it tonight.
>
> Regards,
> The Publisher
>
> P.S. I'm keeping the shurikens.

## About

So you fight him for it, on a rooftop shrine above a rainy neon city. Three times in the fight the Publisher puts two
of your features on his desk, and you choose which one to give away. He fights back with that very move, and every
cut changes both fighters and the game around them:

- **Full art:** the 3D ronin, neon lights, rain, reflections, particles, the film look.
- **Shape ronin:** the art is cut. Flat light, simple shapes.
- **Greybox:** the engine's bare look, grey floor and plain discs for his attacks.
- **The bean:** what is left of the ronin, with a ball for a weapon.

Your katana stays yours: the cards offer the shurikens, the dash, the parry and the Ultimate. Only his final note,
at the very end, cuts the rest, the katana included. Each cut tears the screen along a neon crack. Knock him down
to zero and everything he took comes back for the final blow. Lose, and you retry from the last cut.

[Trailer: paste the YouTube link here]

## Director's Cut

The theme, twice. In the game, you direct the cut: every steal is your edit, and you decide which feature dies
so the game can ship. Behind the game, we directed the agents: one coding agent wrote all the code test-first,
generators made the art, the voices and the music, and we chose what went in and what did not. The full process
is in the dev log, including what went wrong.

## Controls

| Action | Key |
|---|---|
| Move | W A S D |
| Aim | Mouse (the ronin turns to the cursor) |
| Katana (3-hit series) | Left mouse button |
| Parry | Left mouse button just before a shot lands: it sends the shot back |
| Shurikens (every 4th explodes) | Right mouse button |
| Dash | Space |
| Ultimate (when the meter is full) | E |
| Steal card: give away the left or right feature | A or D, or click the card |
| Retry or play again | R |
| Skip the comic or the intro | Any key or click |
| Menu | Arrows or mouse, Enter to pick, Esc to go back |
| How to play (pauses the fight) | F1 |

![How to play](howtoplay.png)

## Credits

- [Pavlo Vynychenko: direction, design, ... (Team Owner)]
- [Teammate 2: role]
- [Teammate 3: role]

## Tools used

- **Claude Code** (Anthropic, Claude Opus): all C++ code written test-first (299 automated tests), the tickets,
  builds and packaging, headless asset imports, this page's first draft and the dev log.
- **Unreal Engine 5.8** with its MCP toolsets: the agent drove the editor for the Niagara effects and the poses.
- **fal**: OpenAI GPT Image 2.6 (concepts, the opening comic, the menu skyline, the cover), Tencent Hunyuan3D v3
  (katana, shuriken, cash stack), Meshy 7.1 through fal (the Publisher's model).
- **Meshy** API: the hero's model and rig, animation library clips, the shrine props.
- **ElevenLabs**: sound effects, the music and its stems, the ambient loop, the two designed voices and 26 voiced
  lines.
- **PBRgen**: the wet slate floor material.
- **Hyper3D Rodin** Gen-2.5: the arena's stone lanterns
- **Blender 5.2**, run headless by our scripts: the Publisher's rig rebuild, the clip and export fixes.
- **ffmpeg**, **butler**, clang-format.

## Third-party assets

No marketplace assets. AI-generated content is ours and listed in THIRD_PARTY.md of the repository with its tool
and terms. From outside:

- Unreal Engine 5.8 basic shapes (`/Engine/BasicShapes`): Unreal Engine EULA.
- unreal-mcp-bridge (github.com/exetorius/unreal-mcp-bridge, MIT): a relay between Claude Code and the editor's MCP
  server; a tool, not in the game.

## Made before the jam

Only tooling, no game content (the full list is PREJAM.md in the repository): an empty UE 5.8 C++ project, the build
and test script, packaging scripts, a code-quality check, the export of the agent logs, git hooks, the agent's rules
(CLAUDE.md, a C++ standard), the MCP setup, a rules brief and the team's plan (text only). Every pre-jam commit
carries the prefix "pre-jam:".

---

Real frames from the game at 1920x1080 (the fight frames from the session-5t build, the HOW TO PLAY screen from
session-5u):

- Banner (960x300): `banner.png`, the full-art fight and the greybox split by the neon crack, with the cover's logo.
- `screens/1_full_art_fight.png`: the full-art fight, the Publisher's beam and the cash.
- `screens/2_steal_card.png`: THE PUBLISHER HAS NOTES, the steal card.
- `screens/3_the_cut.png`: the neon crack tearing the screen mid-cut.
- `screens/4_greybox_bean.png`: the greybox tier, the bean against the Publisher.
- `screens/5_how_to_play.png`: the HOW TO PLAY screen.
